2.review_status: Newly available author manuscript; consequential methods reviewed
2.Cancer_cohort: Breast cell lines; Cisplatin-1/2 TNBC; TCGA ovarian and triple-negative breast
2.N: Cisplatin-1 27 profiled; Cisplatin-2 26 after ASCAT/purity; TCGA OV 218; TCGA breast 78; cell-line assay Ns vary
2.Input_datatype: Allele-specific copy number and allelic imbalance
2.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: Platinum response and BRCA1/2 status; NtAI is evaluated as a scar biomarker
2.LOH_definition: Not a standalone LOH endpoint; copy-neutral LOH is explicitly recognized as a possible source of telomeric AI
2.TAI_definition: Unequal allele copy number with at least one allele present, extending to the subtelomere without crossing the centromere
2.Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: AROMAv2/CalMaTe; TumorBoost with paired normal; ASCAT
2.Purity_ploidy_correction: ASCAT correction; samples below 36% purity and failed profiles excluded in the reported cohorts
2.CNV_method: AROMAv2/CalMaTe; TumorBoost when paired normal available; ASCAT corrects purity/ploidy
2.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: Methylation IDAT/M/U absent; SNP-array allele-intensity/genotype input required
2.Calibration_uncertainty: No formal probability calibration or individual uncertainty interval
2.Validation_strategy: Multiple trials, cell-line datasets, and TCGA cohorts; no predictive-model CV
2.Performance_metrics: ROC AUC/rank tests and platinum-response associations; exact values by cohort
2.Single_sample_compatible: Yes after validated allele-specific profiling and QC
2.Major_strengths: Exact TAI definition and purity/ploidy-aware allele inference across platforms
2.Major_limitations: Platform-dependent probe thresholds; low-purity failures; historical scar can persist after repair restoration
2.Implementation_ideas: Use as truth fixture: AI means unequal allele copy with at least one allele present; telomeric region reaches subtelomere without crossing centromere
2.documented_fact: TAI was derived from SNP-array allele signals with ASCAT, not total CN. Copy-neutral LOH is explicitly a possible source of telomeric AI.
2.inference: Neither ordinary beta values nor methylation-derived total CN contains the demonstrated input needed for canonical TAI.
2.recommendation: Retain canonical TAI only for allele-aware reference data; call total-CN telomeric features telomeric CN alteration burden.

3.review_status: Newly available author manuscript; main methods reviewed, component supplement unavailable
3.Cancer_cohort: Three neoadjuvant TNBC platinum trials; independent breast/ovarian threshold cohort
3.N: Threshold cohort 497 breast + 561 ovarian (268 BRCA1/2-deficient); PrECOG evaluable 70; pooled cisplatin evaluable 50
3.Assay: 54,091-SNP custom NGS panel; MIP SNP array for 10 PrECOG cases
3.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: HRD-high if score >42 and/or deleterious BRCA1/2 mutation
3.HRD_calculation_method: Unweighted HRD-LOH + TAI + LST; individual algorithm details deferred to supplement/prior papers
3.LOH_definition: Component algorithm deferred to supplement/prior paper in the local manuscript
3.LST_definition: Component algorithm deferred to supplement/prior paper in the local manuscript
3.TAI_definition: Component algorithm deferred to supplement/prior paper in the local manuscript
3.Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: Allelic-imbalance profiles from a 54,091-SNP targeted sequencing panel; MIP array for 10 cases
3.Purity_ploidy_correction: Not reported in sufficient detail in the reviewed local main text
3.CNV_method: Allelic-imbalance profiles from targeted SNP reads; platform correlation 0.94 in 31 paired samples
3.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: No methylation-array input; targeted SNP read counts/allelic profiles required
3.Calibration_uncertainty: Cutoff selected independently; no individual prediction interval or cross-cancer calibration
3.Model_class: Prespecified additive scar score; logistic association analyses
3.Training_strategy: Threshold set independent of therapy cohorts; cutoff chosen at fifth percentile of BRCA-deficient scores
3.Validation_strategy: Three clinical trial cohorts with prespecified cisplatin analysis
3.External_validation: Two pooled cisplatin trials separate from threshold cohort
3.Performance_metrics: AUC 0.761 for RCB0/I and 0.747 for pCR; sensitivity at 42 was 85% and 93%
3.Cross_cancer_compatible: Threshold derived in breast/ovarian; no pan-cancer validation
3.Code_software: Commercial assay details partly in supplement/prior paper
3.Major_strengths: Independent threshold cohort and explicit component sum
3.Major_limitations: Commercial pipeline details incomplete locally; treatment prediction and current HR function are distinct
3.Direct_relevance_KIDS26: Defines the reference endpoint and demonstrates independent thresholding
3.Implementation_ideas: Keep continuous sum primary; store cutoff provenance separately
3.documented_fact: The canonical combined score is an unweighted allele-aware LOH+TAI+LST sum. The clinical cutoff was trained in breast/ovarian BRCA-deficient tumors, not pediatric CNS tumors.
3.inference: A value of 42 is not automatically portable across cancers or assays.
3.recommendation: Predict continuous reference HRDsum and do not emit an HRD-high probability without tumor-specific calibration.

4.review_status: Newly available full article; methods/results reviewed
4.Cancer_cohort: Prospective primary stage I-III breast cancer multi-region sampling
4.N: 99 biopsies from 33 tumors; 81 biopsies/32 cancers analyzed; 70 HRD scores from 31 patients
4.Assay: 54,091-SNP NGS capture plus BRCA1/2 and BRCA1 promoter methylation
4.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: HRD score >=42 or tumor BRCA mutation
4.HRD_calculation_method: LOH (>15 Mb subchromosomal) + TAI (to subtelomere, not centromere crossing) + LST (breaks between >10 Mb regions after removing <3 Mb regions)
4.LST_definition: Breaks between adjacent regions greater than 10 Mb after removing regions smaller than 3 Mb
4.TAI_definition: Allelic imbalance extending to a subtelomere without crossing the centromere
4.Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: Hidden Markov segmentation of a 54,091-SNP targeted panel; algorithm similar to Popova
4.Purity_ploidy_correction: Not reported in sufficient detail in the reviewed article
4.CNV_method: Hidden Markov segmentation; allele-specific CN algorithm similar to Popova
4.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: No methylation-array input; SNP allelic read profiles required
4.Calibration_uncertainty: Intraclass correlation reported; no model probability calibration or individual intervals
4.Methylation_preprocessing: BRCA1 promoter: quantitative NGS at 10 CpGs; array methylation not used
4.Validation_strategy: Three spatial biopsies per tumor where material passed
4.Performance_metrics: Patient-level HRD score intraclass correlation 0.977; category/BRCA status perfect concordance in available biopsies
4.Major_limitations: Small single-center cohort and commercial assay
4.Direct_relevance_KIDS26: Supports patient grouping and distinguishes within-tumor from between-tumor variation
4.Implementation_ideas: Group all patient/model-lineage specimens; never split related biopsies across folds
4.documented_fact: Allele-aware HRDsum was spatially reproducible in this small breast cohort, but only 31 patients had scores.
4.inference: Lineage grouping remains mandatory even when scar scores appear stable within one adult tumor type.
4.recommendation: Keep patient/lineage grouped validation; do not treat related PBTP models as independent.

7.review_status: Newly available author manuscript; main methods/results reviewed
7.Cancer_cohort: High-grade serous ovarian cancer: BriTROC-1, PCAWG-OV, TCGA-OV
7.N: BriTROC 142 patients/300 samples; 91 high-quality discovery profiles; PCAWG 112; TCGA 415
7.Assay: Shallow WGS, deep WGS, and SNP array
7.Input_datatype: Absolute total-CN segments and breakpoint-derived distributions
7.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: Signatures associated with mutational processes including HRD; not canonical HRDsum
7.LOH_definition: Absent; total/absolute CN signatures are the target representation
7.LST_definition: Absent; breakpoint distributions are not named canonical LST
7.Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: Battenberg used as a paired WGS check; external TCGA/PCAWG absolute CN includes ABSOLUTE/Battenberg sources
7.Purity_ploidy_correction: QDNAseq plus TP53-VAF probabilistic purity/ploidy/absolute-CN fit; matched WGS checks
7.CNV_method: QDNAseq plus TP53-VAF probabilistic absolute-CN fit for sWGS; Battenberg paired check; ABSOLUTE for external cohorts
7.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: No methylation arrays; sequencing read-depth inputs
7.Calibration_uncertainty: NMF stability and null permutations reported; no individual predictive interval
7.Feature_selection: Six CN distributions: segment size, breaks/10 Mb, adjacent CN change, segment CN, breaks/arm, oscillating-CN run length
7.Training_strategy: 36 mixture components; seven signatures chosen using 1,000 NMF starts and 1,000 permuted nulls
7.Validation_strategy: Independent PCAWG-OV and TCGA-OV decompositions; matched sWGS/WGS purity/ploidy in 34 samples
7.Performance_metrics: Median signature-weight correlation 0.86 across external cohorts; survival test C-index 0.56
7.Single_sample_compatible: Exposure assignment possible after signatures fixed
7.Cross_cancer_compatible: Not demonstrated; HGSOC signatures expected to expand in other cancers
7.Code_software: QDNAseq, Battenberg, ABSOLUTE, FlexMix, NMF, YAPSA
7.Major_strengths: Explicit resolution/purity/ploidy QC and independent CN-platform checks
7.Major_limitations: Total-CN process signatures are assay/pipeline/ploidy sensitive and not canonical allele-aware scars
7.Implementation_ideas: Borrow segment/breakpoint distributions only after conumee2 benchmark; record callable denominator and ploidy
7.documented_fact: The seven signatures were derived from total/absolute CN features with strong quality filtering; the paper explicitly warns that preprocessing and ploidy alter signatures.
7.inference: This supports a total-CN structural branch but cannot recover LOH or TAI without alleles.
7.recommendation: Keep total-CN features secondary and name them as structural/CN signatures, not HRDsum components.

12.local_file: ../papers/BJOG - 2022 - Yuan - Genomic Scar Score  A robust model predicting homologous recombination deficiency based on genomic.pdf
12.review_status: Newly available full article; methods/results reviewed
12.Cancer_cohort: Ovarian and breast development; ovarian PARPi cohort
12.N: 377 unique development/test patients (305 on 24K, 203 on 72K, 131 overlapping); training extremes 96; independent extreme test 89; PARPi cohort 58
12.Input_datatype: Sequenza allele-specific CN, BAF, purity and ploidy
12.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: gBRCA biallelic deficiency versus quiescent genomes for SVM training
12.HRD_calculation_method: GSS is an SVM probability from 28 categorized allele-specific CN features; not LOH+LST+TAI HRDsum
12.LOH_definition: Not a canonical standalone component; LOH-related event categories enter the 28-feature SVM
12.LST_definition: Not a canonical standalone component; breakpoints enter the feature set
12.Upstream_allele_specific_CN_method: Sequenza v3 on hg19 using read depth and B-allele frequency
12.Purity_ploidy_correction: Sequenza estimates purity and ploidy; values are explicit inputs/context
12.CNV_method: Sequenza v3 hg19, default parameters, read depth plus BAF
12.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: No methylation arrays; 24K/72K SNP-capture reads required
12.Calibration_uncertainty: SVM probability used; formal calibration and individual uncertainty not reported
12.Feature_selection: CN events by length/site/type plus breakpoints; features retained only if occurrence count exceeded training N
12.Training_strategy: Penalty C chosen by three-fold internal CV; extremes used for training
12.Validation_strategy: Independent BRCA-deficient/quiescent test; panel concordance; separate PARPi outcome cohort
12.Performance_metrics: 24K test AUC 0.996, accuracy 95.5%; 24K/72K r=0.89; PARPi PFS 9.4 vs 4.4 months
12.Single_sample_compatible: Yes with the validated SNP panel and frozen SVM
12.Code_software: BWA, GATK, MuTect2, ANNOVAR, Sequenza, scikit-learn 0.22.1
12.Major_strengths: Interpretable allele-specific CN features and cross-panel comparison
12.Major_limitations: Extreme-group design inflates discrimination; no pediatric/cancer-held-out transfer; probability scale differs from HRDsum
12.Direct_relevance_KIDS26: Serious secondary model comparator if allele-aware data are available
12.Implementation_ideas: Do not port its features to methylation total CN; possible WGS-reference comparator after development
12.documented_fact: Despite broad wording about chromosomal CN, the model requires Sequenza BAF-derived allele-specific CN and purity/ploidy.
12.inference: Its high AUC does not show canonical scars can be obtained from methylation total CN.
12.recommendation: Do not replace elastic-net CpG regression; consider only as an allele-aware genomic comparator.

15.review_status: Newly available consensus article; recommendations and validation sections reviewed
15.Cancer_cohort: Scoping review of human tissue studies plus international laboratory survey
15.N: 140 survey respondents (61 performing/validating HRD); 62 reviewed studies assessed HRR promoter methylation
15.Ground_truth_HRD_definition: No universal definition; components and composite must be declared
15.LOH_definition: Consensus requires the laboratory to state the operational definition; no single universal rule imposed
15.LST_definition: Consensus requires the laboratory to state the operational definition; no single universal rule imposed
15.TAI_definition: Consensus requires the laboratory to state the operational definition; no single universal rule imposed
15.Purity_ploidy_correction: Specimen and tumor-content requirements must be validated and reported; no single caller prescribed
15.Raw_IDAT_MU_requirement: Not applicable; multiple assay families considered
15.Calibration_uncertainty: Tumor-specific cutoffs and individual/composite performance should be validated; no universal calibration
15.Model_class: Consensus recommendations, not a predictive model
15.Validation_strategy: Double-reviewed scoping extraction, survey, external review and consensus vote
15.Single_sample_compatible: Guidance applies to clinical single-sample assays
15.Cross_cancer_compatible: Requires tumor-specific cutoffs or explicit insufficient-evidence statement
15.Major_limitations: Does not establish clinical utility or validate methylation-to-HRDsum prediction
15.Implementation_ideas: Record tumor content, comparator use, loci/distribution, components, algorithm, cutoff provenance and individual/composite performance
15.documented_fact: The consensus recommends declaring specimen/tumor-content requirements, validating BRCA-wild-type HRD-positive samples, documenting each scar and its detection method, and using tumor-specific cutoffs. BRCA1/RAD51C promoter methylation may be considered, but relevant thresholds remain unclear.
15.inference: A pan-cancer binary threshold or unlabeled composite would be scientifically weak for KIDS26.
15.recommendation: Keep continuous output primary; add assay provenance and tumor-specific cutoff warnings; make promoter methylation an orthogonal annotation.
